Q: What is a mesh topology?
Option1: A network where each node connects directly to every other node
Option2: A network with a single central hub
Option4: A layered core and access design

Q: What is a full mesh topology?
Option1: Every node is directly connected to every other node
Option2: Some nodes have direct connections, others rely on intermediaries
Option3: A central hub connects all devices
Option4: Two layers of switches connect end devices

Q: What is a partial mesh topology?
Option1: Only some nodes have direct links to others
Option2: Every node has a direct connection to every other
Option3: A single backbone links all devices

Q: Which is an advantage of a full mesh topology?
Option1: High redundancy and fault tolerance

Q: Which is a disadvantage of a full mesh topology?
Option1: High cabling and hardware costs

Q: What is a hybrid topology?
Option1: A network combining features of two or more topologies
Option2: A wireless network with mixed frequencies
Option3: A topology using only fiber connections
Option4: A topology limited to star and bus layouts

Q: What is the main benefit of a hybrid topology?
Option1: Flexibility to optimize for performance and cost

Q: What is a star topology?
Option1: All devices connect to a central hub or switch
Option2: Each device connects to all others
Option4: Devices are connected in a straight line

Q: What is a hub-and-spoke design?
Option1: A central hub connects to multiple branch nodes
Option2: All nodes connect in a ring
Option3: All nodes connect to each other
Option4: Nodes are connected in a mesh

Q: Which is a major disadvantage of a star topology?
Option1: Central device failure affects all nodes
Option2: High cabling cost for short distances

Q: What is a spine-and-leaf topology?
Option1: A data center design where each leaf switch connects to every spine switch
Option2: A layered model with three tiers

Q: What is the main advantage of a spine-and-leaf topology?
Option1: Predictable low-latency paths between any two endpoints

Q: What is a point-to-point connection?
Option1: A direct link between two devices
Option2: A network with one hub and many spokes
Option3: A topology where all nodes are connected

Q: What is a three-tier hierarchical model?
Option1: A network design with core, distribution, and access layers
Option2: A design with three mesh nodes
Option3: A wireless design with three APs
Option4: A topology with three points of connection

Q: What is the core layer in the three-tier model responsible for?
Option1: Fast transport of large amounts of data between distribution layers

Q: What is the distribution layer in the three-tier model responsible for?
Option1: Routing and policy-based connectivity between core and access layers

Q: What is the access layer in the three-tier model responsible for?
Option1: Connecting end devices to the network

Q: What is a collapsed core architecture?
Option1: Combining core and distribution functions into a single layer

Q: What is north-south traffic flow?
Option1: Data moving between clients and servers, often crossing network boundaries
Option2: Traffic between devices in the same rack
Option3: Traffic moving within a single VLAN

Q: What is east-west traffic flow?
Option1: Data moving between devices within the same data center or layer

Q: Which topology provides the highest redundancy?
Option1: Full mesh

Q: Which topology is typically most cost-effective for small branch offices?
Option1: Hub-and-spoke

Q: In a data center, which topology is preferred for predictable low latency between any two servers?
Option1: Spine-and-leaf

Q: Which design collapses core and distribution layers into one?
Option1: Collapsed core

Q: Which traffic flow is most likely between two servers in the same rack?
Option1: East-west

Q: A company needs a topology that mixes wireless mesh for one department and star topology for another. What is this called?
Option1: Hybrid

Q: A small office with one switch and all PCs connected to it is using which topology?
Option1: Star

Q: A wide-area network connecting several branch offices to a central HQ uses which design?
Option1: Hub-and-spoke

Q: A direct fiber link between two data centers is an example of which topology?
Option1: Point-to-point

Q: In a partial mesh, why might some devices not connect directly to all others?
Option1: To reduce cost while maintaining some redundancy

Q: Which layer of the three-tier model connects directly to end devices?
Option1: Access

Q: Which type of traffic is most impacted by firewall inspection at the network edge?
Option1: North-south

Q: Which topology can be either full or partial depending on redundancy needs?
Option1: Mesh

Q: Which design is especially popular in modern leaf-spine data centers?
Option1: Spine-and-leaf
